accepted.question_text: Let X1, X2, and X3 be observed random variables that each take four states, and let Y be a hidden four-state random variable, so that the joint distribution of (X1, X2, X3) is represented by a 4×4×4 table (p_ijk) lying in the 64-dimensional tensor space C^4 ⊗ C^4 ⊗ C^4. Equivalently, this is the variety of 4×4×4 tensors of rank at most 4, also described as the naive Bayes model, the conditional independence model [X1 ⟂⟂ X2 ⟂⟂ X3 | Y], or the third secant variety of P^3 × P^3 × P^3. Do the known polynomial invariants of degrees 5 and 9 suffice to cut out this variety set-theoretically or ideally?

evidence.quote: Consider the variety of 4 × 4 × 4-tables of tensor rank at most 4. Do the known polynomial invariants of degree five and nine suffice to cut out this variety?

• the set of 4 × 4 × 4-tables of tensor rank ≤ 4 • mixture of independent random variables • the naive Bayes model • the CI model [X1 ⊥⊥ X2 ⊥⊥ X3 | Y ]. • third secant variety of Segre variety P3 × P3 × P3

accepted.question_text: For the 4×4×4 hidden-variable model whose coordinates are p_ijk with i, j, k ∈ {A, C, G, T} and whose parametrization is p_ijk = ρ_Ai σ_Aj θ_Ak + ρ_Ci σ_Cj θ_Ck + ρ_Gi σ_Gj θ_Gk + ρ_Ti σ_Tj θ_Tk, determine the homogeneous prime ideal I of polynomial relations among the 64 coordinates in the ring Q[p_AAA, p_AAC, p_AAT, ..., p_TTG, p_TTT].

evidence.quote: Our problem is to compute its homogeneous prime ideal I in the polynomial ring with 64 unknowns, Q[pAAA, pAAC, pAAT, . . . , pTTG, pTTT].

accepted.question_text: Develop the geometry and commutative algebra of graphical models with hidden random variables by constructing the associated varieties from familiar secant varieties and by using representation-theoretic methods. In particular, the task is to understand these hidden-variable graphical-model varieties as algebraic varieties assembled from known secant constructions and then analyzed with tools from representation theory.

evidence.quote: Study the geometry and commutative algebra of graphical models with hidden random variables. Construct these varieties by gluing familiar secant varieties, and by applying representation theory.

accepted.question_text: Characterize all projective varieties M for which the maximum likelihood degree equals 1, where the maximum likelihood degree is the number of critical points, for generic data, of the likelihood function restricted to M after excluding poles and zeros. Equivalently, determine exactly which algebraic statistical models have a rational maximum likelihood estimator in this sense.

evidence.quote: Characterize all projective varieties whose maximum likelihood degree is equal to one.

The maximum likelihood degree of a model M is the number of critical points of the restriction to M of L = p0^u0 · p1^u1 · p2^u2 · · · pn^un / (p0 + p1 + · · · + pn)^(u0 + u1 + ··· + un). Here we only count critical points that are not poles or zeros, and u0, u1, . . . , un are assumed to be generic.

accepted.question_text: For the determinantal variety consisting of m×n matrices of rank at most r, determine its maximum likelihood degree, meaning the number of nonzero, nonpole critical points of the likelihood function on that model for generic data.

evidence.quote: Open Problem. Determine the ML degree of the variety of m × n-matrices of rank ≤ r.
The maximum likelihood degree of a model M is the number of critical points of the restriction to M of L = p0^u0 · p1^u1 · p2^u2 · · · pn^un / (p0 + p1 + · · · + pn)^(u0 + u1 + ··· + un).

accepted.question_text: In the model of positive 4×4 matrices (p_ij) of rank at most 2 that is used for the DiaNA DNA-sequence example, decide whether the specific matrix p̂_ij = (1/40) [[3,3,2,2],[3,3,2,2],[2,2,3,3],[2,2,3,3]] maximizes the likelihood function L = (∏_i p_ii)^4 (∏_{i ≠ j} p_ij)^2 (∑_{i,j} p_ij)^(-40).

evidence.quote: True or False: The matrix (p̂ij) = 1/40 [[3 3 2 2] [3 3 2 2] [2 2 3 3] [2 2 3 3]] maximizes L = (∏i pii)^4 (∏i≠j pij)^2 (∑i,j pij)^−40.

accepted.question_text: Which collections of almost-principal minors [i ⟂⟂ j | K] can simultaneously vanish for a positive definite symmetric 5×5 covariance matrix Σ? Here [i ⟂⟂ j | K] denotes the determinant of the submatrix with row indices {i} ∪ K and column indices {j} ∪ K, and its vanishing is equivalent to conditional independence of variable i and variable j given the joint variable K in a multivariate Gaussian model.

evidence.quote: Which sets of almost-principal minors can be zero for a positive definite symmetric 5 × 5-matrix?

An almost-principal minor of Σ has row indices {i} ∪ K and column indices {j} ∪ K for some K ⊂ [n] and i, j ∈ [n]\K. It is denoted [i⊥⊥ j |K ]. Lemma. The determinant [i⊥⊥ j |K ] is zero if and only if the random variable i is independent of the random variable j given the joint random variable K.

accepted.question_text: Determine which semigraphoids are realizable by multivariate Gaussian random variables, equivalently which conditional-independence structures can occur for Gaussian conditional independence models inside the cone of positive semidefinite covariance matrices.

evidence.quote: Study the geometry of conditional independence models for multivariate Gaussian random variables. Which semigraphoids can be realized by Gaussians?
A Gaussian conditional independence model is a subvariety of PSDn defined by equations [i⊥⊥ j |K ] = 0.

accepted.question_text: Characterize the image of the entropy map H: SDP_n → SubMod_n that sends a positive definite matrix to the logarithms of all 2^n principal minors. Here SubMod_n is the polyhedral cone of vectors satisfying the submodular inequalities H_{ {i}∪K } + H_{ {j}∪K } ≤ H_{ {i,j}∪K } + H_K.

evidence.quote: Taking the logarithms of all 2^n principal minors of any positive definite matrix defines the entropy map H : SDPn → SubModn.
Problem: Characterize the image of H.

accepted.question_text: Let X1, X2, ..., Xn be discrete random variables with d1, d2, ..., dn states, and let a chosen collection of conditional-independence statements define a determinantal variety in C^{d1} ⊗ C^{d2} ⊗ ··· ⊗ C^{dn}. The corresponding strict conditional-independence variety consists of those tables for which exactly the chosen conditional-independence statements hold and all other conditional-independence statements fail. Does every such strict conditional-independence variety have a Q-rational point? What can be said in the regime where d1, d2, ..., dn are all sufficiently large?
accepted.context_brief: Rational points on strict CI varieties

evidence.quote: Any collection of CI statements defines a determinantal variety in the space of tables, C^d1 ⊗ C^d2 ⊗ · · · ⊗ C^dn. The corresponding strict CI variety is the set of tables for which the given CI statements hold but all other CI statement do not hold.
Problem: Does every strict CI variety have a Q-rational point? What if d1, d2, . . . , dn ≫ 0 ?
